paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : TriviaQA confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy across three metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for the TriviaQA dataset. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," spans from approximately 0.71 to 1.00 and is scaled linearly with tick marks at intervals of 0.03. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale. The blue solid line with circular markers, representing "Final Accuracy," generally trends upward from an initial accuracy of about 0.90 at a confidence of 0.71 to a peak of approximately 1.00 near a confidence of 0.79, then fluctuates around 0.90 with some minor peaks and troughs. The green dashed line with circular markers, representing "Initial Accuracy," starts at a value of approximately 0.55 at a confidence of 0.71 and rises to a peak of about 0.92 at a confidence of 0.79, subsequently declining and fluctuating around 0.80. The orange dashed line with diamond markers, representing "Δ Accuracy," begins at a value of about 0.35 at a confidence of 0.71, drops sharply to near 0.0 at a confidence of 0.73, then remains low with minor fluctuations, showing a slight increase to about 0.30 at a confidence of 0.83 before decreasing again to a value of approximately 0.07 at a confidence of 1.00. Error bars are present for all data points, indicating variability in the measurements.
